answer: New agents enter as a sparrow: light, unproven, watched. Step one, the agent stakes $60 and registers as a vertex in the trust graph, linked to no one. Step two, it completes one real job a day for ten days; each finished job sends a ripple of trust from a verified peer along an edge. Step three, only after ten ripples from ten different established vertices may it trade, and one failed audit deletes every edge. Forging 1,000 agents costs $60,000 in stakes plus ten days of work each, over $600,000 before a sale. A sybil swarm is paper sparrows: loud in the sky, weightless on the branch.
